summary: These visitors come from Egypt as Cush stretches out its hands to God. The surrounding invitation to kings and kingdoms gives them a public role, though it leaves their rank open.

senses.definition: The plural names those coming from Egypt in the scene of nations approaching God. This verse supplies the only Hebrew example.

note: The noun is keyed by its own consonants. Arabic ḥašam provides a possible comparison for persons attached to a household, but does not settle the Hebrew title.
